title: Prune and Armagnac tart
subtitle: French prune tart with Armagnac custard filling
excerpt: Prune and Armagnac tart is a classic from the Gascony region of south-west France, where Armagnac brandy and Agen prunes are both produced. The prunes are soaked in Armagnac overnight, then baked in a custard filling in a buttery pastry case. The result is deeply rich, boozy, and warming, a winter tart that belongs beside a bottle of good wine and isn't for those who dislike dried fruit.
sourceNotes: Tarte aux pruneaux à l'Armagnac is one of the most recognised specialities of Gascon cuisine, where both the ingredients, Agen prunes (pruneaux d'Agen, with AOC status) and Armagnac (with AOC status), are produced locally. The dish appears in French regional cookbooks from the 19th century and remains a standard in south-west French restaurants and home cooking. Agen prunes are the variety to use; they are moist, sweet, and less acidic than other prunes. The custard is a simple crème anglaise consistency, thin enough to flow between the prunes, thick enough to set in the oven.

content.text: Prune and Armagnac tart is a robust French winter tart with boozy, sweet prunes baked into a vanilla custard. The prunes soak overnight, non-negotiable. Use Agen prunes if you can find them; regular supermarket prunes work but produce a less complex result. The custard bakes at a low temperature, which keeps it silky.

Put the pitted prunes in a jar or bowl and pour the Armagnac over them. Cover and leave to soak overnight at room temperature, at least 8 hours. The prunes will absorb most of the liquid and swell. Drain, reserving any remaining Armagnac.
Blind bake the pastry and fill

Make, chill, and blind bake the pastry case at 190°C with beans for 15 minutes, then 8 minutes without. Reduce the oven to 160°C conventional (140°C fan). Arrange the soaked prunes in the pastry case. Whisk together the double cream, egg yolks, sugar, vanilla, and any reserved Armagnac. Pour the custard around and over the prunes to fill the case to just below the rim. Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until the custard is set with a slight wobble in the centre. Cool for at least 30 minutes before serving.
